papers.title: The Asymmetrical Architecture of Ultradian REM Sleep: Direction, NREM Currency, and a Finite Post-REM Predictive Horizon in Mice
papers.summary: The study reanalysed 24-hour recordings from 25 mice to test directionality in ultradian REM sleep organisation, using mixed-effects models, quantile regression, hazard models, and held-out-mouse comparisons. It reports that preceding REM duration predicted subsequent NREM accumulation positively (rho=0.506) across all animals, while accumulated NREM did not predict subsequent REM duration; the REMpre effect became undetectable beyond about 10 minutes of accumulated NREM, supporting an asymmetrical graded refractory regime.

papers.title: EEGDM: Label-Efficient EEG Representation Learning with Generative Diffusion Model.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposed EEGDM, a diffusion-based EEG representation learning framework with a Structured State-Space Model for Diffusion Pretraining (SSMDP) and Latent Fusion Module (LFM). Across TUEV, CHB-MIT, and IIIC benchmarks, EEGDM achieved competitive or superior performance versus state-of-the-art methods, including EEG foundation models, while requiring substantially fewer pretraining and downstream samples.

papers.title: A semi-automated genetic screen using genome-wide association analysis identifies modulators of stress-induced sleep in Caenorhabditis elegans.
papers.summary: The paper performed a semi-automated screen of 940 whole-genome sequenced Million Mutation Project strains using robotic automation, high-throughput imaging, and genome-wide association analysis to identify modulators of stress-induced sleep (SIS) in Caenorhabditis elegans. The authors identified three genes (strd-1, cla-1, and egl-8) whose mutations reproducibly influence SIS and established a pipeline for automated behavioral phenotyping coupled with gene-based association.

papers.title: Biophysical modeling of thalamocortical circuit dynamics: species-specific insights into neural synchrony, sleep spindles, and circuit mechanisms.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: A biophysically-grounded computational model incorporating core and matrix thalamocortical pathways, thalamic interneurons, and open/closed/hybrid reticular-thalamic loop configurations was used to investigate species-specific thalamocortical dynamics. Primate-like circuits showed greater stability and synchrony with more regular spindles, whereas rodent-like circuits were more sensitive to parameter changes and exhibited greater variability in spindle structure and timing.

papers.title: TEFAR: a lightweight, configurable framework for semi-automatic artefact component classification in EEG and TMS-EEG
papers.summary: Introduces TEFAR, a lightweight, configurable FieldTrip-based framework for semi-automatic ICA component classification of artefacts in ordinary EEG and TMS-EEG, using spectral, spatial, and temporal signatures with robust median/MAD thresholds. In 30 ground-truth simulations, TEFAR achieved specificity 1.000 and sensitivity 0.96-0.97 for both profiles; application to real EEG/TMS-EEG recordings is pending.

papers.title: Intermittent Cranial Accelerometric Pulses - a Potential Marker of Neurodegenerative Disease
papers.summary: This paper identifies a novel phenomenon called Sleep Bursts (SBs), brief periodic bursts in cranial forces during sleep, characterized in healthy subjects and those with neurodegenerative disease (NDD). SBs occurred at lower rates in NDD subjects, with reduced EEG delta power, suggesting a potential marker for neurodegenerative disease and a possible link to glymphatic drainage.

papers.title: Anesthesia-Informed Approaches to Insomnia: Shared Neural Circuits, Biomimetic Sleep, and Emerging Interventional Strategies.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines convergent neural circuits underlying anesthesia-induced and physiological sleep, appraises evidence for anesthetic agents (dexmedetomidine, ketamine/esketamine, propofol) delivered through non-traditional modalities, and evaluates perioperative sleep optimization for insomnia. It concludes that anesthesia-informed approaches provide mechanistic insights and investigational directions rather than established alternatives to CBT-I or approved hypnotics, highlighting the need for adequately powered insomnia-specific RCTs.

papers.title: Hot take on a cool topic: is there really a need for a systemic master mediator of metabolic suppression in mouse daily torpor?
papers.summary: This perspective argues that daily torpor in mice, induced by caloric restriction and cool environment, does not require a dedicated master mediator for systemic metabolic rate suppression. Instead, centrally mediated changes including cessation of physical activity, reduced thermogenesis, lowered defended minimum body temperature, and reduced cardiovascular work drive the 75-80% drop in metabolic rate, with temperature-dependent effects on biochemical reaction rates accounting for much of the further reduction.

papers.title: CircadiOmics: bioinformatics platform for circadian rhythms.
papers.summary: CircadiOmics is a bioinformatics platform and repository for circadian omic data, containing 704 omic datasets across 18 species, 30 tissue/organ categories, and 21 experiment types. The updated version provides tools for comparing and visualizing molecular-level circadian oscillations using BIO_CYCLE-computed periodicity statistics (period, amplitude, phase, p-values, q-values) available as interactive plots and downloadable tables.

papers.title: A Patient-Specific Framework for Separating Temporal Localization from Intracranial Waveform Reconstruction of Interictal Epileptiform Discharges from Scalp EEG
papers.summary: The study developed a patient-specific dual-branch convolutional-attention framework to separate temporal localization from event-specific intracranial waveform reconstruction of interictal epileptiform discharges from scalp EEG in six subjects with simultaneous high-density scalp EEG and intracranial EEG. Results showed that scalp EEG contained recoverable temporal information in some subjects (where accuracy 0.080-0.984, mean 0.333 vs. chance 0.125), but event-specific single-contact morphology was not consistently recovered beyond a fixed patient-specific template (mean waveform correlation 0.752 for model vs. 0.754 for template).

papers.title: Effect of R-R interval normalization on frequency domain analysis of heart rate variability during sleep.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effect of R-R interval normalization on frequency-domain heart rate variability parameters during sleep in 130 participants. Normalization significantly improved differentiation of sleep stages and enhanced slow-wave sleep detection, with the area under the curve for high-frequency-based detection increasing from 0.50 to 0.86.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Assessment of Sleepiness from Fingertip Pulse Wave Analysis During Objective Daytime Testing.
papers.summary: Tested a deep learning sleep-staging model on fingertip photoplethysmography (PPG) for assessing daytime sleepiness in MSLT (n=143) and MWT (n=127) datasets. PPG-based sleepiness classification reached 80% accuracy in MSLT and 83% in MWT; sleep probability curves differed significantly between sleepy and non-sleepy groups, but direct zero-shot MWT second-by-second sleep detection was limited (precision 0.10).

papers.title: Sleep and Overnight Cardiovascular Outcomes During the First Week on a Temperature-Controlled Sleep Surface: Stratified by Baseline Performance
papers.summary: In an open-label study of 171 adults, a temperature-controlled sleep surface increased total sleep time and improved overnight cardiovascular measures, with the largest gains observed in those with the poorest baseline sleep. Stratification by baseline performance revealed significant improvements in sleep efficiency, REM, deep sleep, and HRV in the most deficient quartiles.

papers.title: Electrophysiological brain reconfiguration during meditation-induced extended cessation of consciousness: an EEG microstate study
papers.summary: Used dense-sampling EEG microstate analysis in five highly trained meditators to characterize brain dynamics during meditation-induced extended cessation (EC) versus counting and memory control tasks. EC was associated with reduced self-related microstate B, increased integrative microstate C, and rerouting of sensory-related microstate A toward integrative rather than self-related processing across multiple frequency bands.

papers.title: Multidomain Electroencephalography Biomarker Fusion for Machine Learning-Based Dementia Classification.
papers.summary: This study evaluated multidomain EEG biomarkers for classifying Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls using a Random Forest classifier with explainable AI. The full model achieved 96% training and 92% test accuracy; removing entropy features increased test accuracy to 94%, with entropy showing the lowest classification contribution.

papers.title: Behavioural thermoregulation modulates circadian clock gene expression in juvenile Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar).
papers.summary: Juvenile Atlantic salmon kept in a thermal gradient showed robust daily rhythms of thermal preference and significant circadian oscillations in clock gene expression in brain, proximal intestine, and distal intestine. Thermal choice enhanced clock gene expression in both intestinal regions, whereas brain responses were more complex, indicating behavioral thermoregulation modulates central and peripheral circadian clocks.

papers.title: The Gut-Brain Axis in Sleep Deprivation: Mechanisms, Dysbiosis, and Potential Therapeutic Avenues.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized human and animal evidence on how sleep deprivation alters gut microbial communities and immune signaling via the gut-brain axis, converging on circadian/microbial misalignment, inflammatory and barrier dysfunction loops, and altered neurotransmitter and metabolite signaling. It discusses probiotics, prebiotics, postbiotics, synbiotics, diet-based short-chain fatty acid strategies, chronobiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation as biologically plausible but still mainly small-trial or preclinical interventions.

papers.title: Exploring multifaceted mental resilience from the perspectives of sleep and circadian rhythm in healthy adults
papers.summary: In 156 healthy adults assessed with 14-day actigraphy, polysomnography, and dim light melatonin onset, partial least squares regression identified a modest but significant association between greater mental resilience and a sleep/circadian profile marked by greater frontal-central NREM slow-wave activity, greater REM frontal theta, lower occipital spectral power, and probably earlier DLMO. The study was cross-sectional and calls for longitudinal and interventional work.

papers.title: AAV-mediated TBR1 supplementation ameliorates behavioral and electrophysiological abnormalities in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice
papers.summary: Evaluated AAV-mediated human TBR1 supplementation in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice after a single postnatal day 3 retroorbital injection (2E11 vector genomes). Treatment increased TBR1 protein and TBR1/CTIP2/parvalbumin cell counts, improved sociability and food-seeking behaviors, and attenuated elevated relative theta power and social-interaction EEG abnormalities, though anterior commissure abnormalities and some EEG/sleep deficits persisted.

papers.title: Predicting the immediate and subsequent effects of commercials on product valuation using EEG and deep learning
papers.summary: EEG data from 161 participants watching commercials were analyzed with deep learning to predict willingness to pay and ad liking. Deep learning on raw neural data achieved substantially higher predictive accuracy than standard EEG measures and generalized to new participants and products, though performance declined as generalization demands increased and value differences narrowed.

papers.title: Ramadan fasting and thyroid function: a narrative review of physiological adaptation and clinical management.
papers.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes evidence on Ramadan fasting and thyroid function in healthy, hypothyroid, and hyperthyroid individuals. It reports that Ramadan fasting preserves hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis function in healthy adults, may increase post-Ramadan TSH in levothyroxine-treated hypothyroid patients with stable FT4, and that evidence in hyperthyroidism is limited and based on expert opinion.

papers.title: Timing of Device-Measured Physical Activity and Sleep in Relation to Meeting Physical Activity Guidelines in U.S. Adults.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2003-2006 accelerometer data (n=3,153) examined whether timing of MVPA and sleep is associated with meeting physical activity guidelines. Morning MVPA and early sleep were independently and jointly associated with higher prevalence of meeting guidelines.

papers.title: Subregion-specific temporal lobe EEG signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: Evidence from high-density EEG.
papers.summary: Resting-state 128-channel high-density EEG in 55 individuals with amnestic mild cognitive impairment and 35 controls revealed increased gamma-band activity across bilateral temporal subregions and elevated delta power and theta/beta ratios mainly in right temporal subregions. Right temporal delta activity was negatively associated with memory performance, and left temporal gamma measures discriminated aMCI comparably to whole-temporal measures.

papers.title: Developmental Environmental Chronotoxicity by Polystyrene Nanoplastics Exacerbates High-Fat Diet-Induced Pediatric MAFLD Through Circadian Disruption and Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
papers.summary: In juvenile but not adult mice, polystyrene nanoplastics exacerbated high-fat diet-induced hepatic steatosis, dyslipidemia, and hepatomegaly without altering energy intake. Mechanistic analyses revealed disruption of the hepatic circadian-mitochondrial axis, including altered clock gene programs, impaired AMPK signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and suppressed oxidative metabolism; AMPK activation by AICAR or circadian modulation by SR9009 alleviated steatosis and mitochondrial defects.

papers.title: Age-dependent associations of sleep duration and insomnia symptoms with cognitive decline across five decades of adult life: a multi-cohort longitudinal study
papers.summary: Multi-cohort longitudinal study of 16,884 participants examined age-specific associations of sleep duration and insomnia symptoms with cognitive decline. Difficulty falling asleep was associated with faster cognitive decline at age 50 but the association attenuated and reversed at older ages, suggesting midlife insomnia may be a modifiable risk factor.

papers.title: Correlation Analysis of Sleep Quality and Heart Rate Variability in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
papers.summary: This prospective observational cohort study of 95 cardiac surgery patients examined correlations between perioperative sleep quality and heart rate variability. It found that patients with poor sleep quality had significantly lower HF, SDNN, SDANN, PNN50, and RMSSD at all time points, and that these HRV parameters were significantly negatively correlated with sleep disturbance, with PNN50 at 1 day postoperatively showing the strongest correlation (r=-0.78).

papers.title: Integrating Behavioral Sleep Medicine with Behavioral Parent Training for Preschool ADHD: Stakeholder Insights for an Early Childhood Intervention.
papers.summary: This qualitative study gathered iterative feedback from parents of preschoolers with elevated ADHD symptoms, pediatricians, and pediatric behavioral health providers on an integrated behavioral parent training and behavioral sleep medicine intervention. Stakeholders emphasized a 24-hour approach, practical developmentally appropriate strategies, caregiver support, and treatment tailoring to family culture and structure.

papers.title: Multimodal predictors of response to intravenous ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: toward personalized treatment in major depressive and bipolar disorders.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided review of 150 studies synthesized multimodal predictors of intravenous ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression, including baseline depressive severity, comorbid anxiety, inflammatory and neuroplastic biomarkers, metabolic factors, genetic variants, neurophysiological signatures, and early symptomatic improvement. It proposes a preliminary clinical framework and pilot questionnaire, while noting that most predictors remain exploratory and require prospective validation.

papers.title: Rates and correlates of nightmares and insomnia in active duty military service members pre- and postdeployment.
papers.journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
papers.summary: U.S. Army personnel were assessed pre- and post-deployment to determine rates and correlates of nightmares and insomnia. Nightmares and insomnia, alone and comorbid, were associated with mental health problems, and chronic postdeployment trajectories were linked to higher PTSD, anger, and anxiety symptoms.

papers.title: Comparison of Surgical Effectiveness Between Conventional and Modified Maxillomandibular Advancement in Adult Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: This retrospective comparison of 24 adult obstructive sleep apnea patients found that modified maxillomandibular advancement (with premolar extraction and segmental osteotomies) and conventional maxillomandibular advancement achieved comparable postoperative polysomnographic and upper-airway outcomes, despite the modified group having more severe baseline apnea-hypopnea and respiratory disturbance indices. The modified technique may be an effective surgical option for patients with dentoalveolar and/or lip protrusion.

papers.title: Current knowledge of intermittent photic stimulation for electroencephalography in dogs.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on intermittent photic stimulation for electroencephalography in dogs, noting that protocols vary substantially in stimulus design, vigilance state, and electrode montage. It proposes a framework for standardized awake testing with defined stimulus parameters and improved spatial sampling to enhance diagnostic sensitivity and translational alignment with human epileptology.

papers.title: Continuous Versus Routine EEG in Critically Ill Patients Without Primary Neurologic Condition: Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: Post hoc analysis of the randomized CERTA trial in 76 critically ill adults without primary neurologic conditions found that continuous EEG versus repeated routine EEG was not associated with differences in 6-month mortality, functional outcome, or detection of seizures/status epilepticus.

papers.title: Social-behavioral and psychological resource advantage and favorable cognitive-domain transitions among older Chinese adults: a longitudinal CHARLS study.
papers.summary: Using five waves of CHARLS data from older Chinese adults, this longitudinal study found that greater social-behavioral and psychological resource advantage was associated with higher odds of recovery from localized cognitive impairment and lower odds of progression to multidomain impairment.

papers.title: Cannabis use and sleep outcomes among National Guard and Reserve soldiers.
papers.summary: Longitudinal study of 485 National Guard and Reserve soldiers examined associations between cannabis use and sleep outcomes over six waves. Current cannabis use was significantly associated with worse global sleep scores and specifically with sleep latency, sleep disturbances, and sleeping medication use.

papers.title: Sodium Valproate-Induced Encephalopathy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Case report of a 63-year-old woman on long-term valproic acid who developed encephalopathy with sinus bradycardia despite normal ammonia and therapeutic valproate levels; discontinuation led to rapid and complete resolution.

papers.title: Generation of a transgenic cephalopod
papers.summary: Generated stable transgenic dwarf cuttlefish (Ascarosepion bandense) expressing ubiquitous nuclear-localized mScarlet using CRISPR and the transposons Sleeping Beauty and Minos. Minos was the most efficient strategy, enabling live imaging of cell dynamics during embryonic development and adaptable for diverse genetic tools.

papers.title: Patterns of Drug Use Across Social and Sexual Contexts in Spain: Insights From the European Web Survey on Drugs 2024.
papers.summary: Analysis of European Web Survey on Drugs 2024 data from 6,399 Spanish participants characterized patterns of drug use across social and sexual contexts. Recreational use was most common (78.0%), with 13.7% reporting drug use to enhance sexual performance/pleasure and 3.3% reporting chemsex; chemsex is increasingly reported among women.

papers.title: Cannabidiol (CBD) differentially shapes systemic cytokines and transcriptomic profiles in the liver and spleen: insights from a male mouse model.
papers.summary: Investigated dose- and time-dependent effects of cannabidiol (CBD) on systemic cytokines and liver/spleen transcriptomes in male C57BL/6J mice. CBD reduced IL-1β and TNF-α after short-term treatment and IL-6 primarily after long-term exposure, with pronounced hepatic transcriptional reprogramming and limited splenic changes, supporting CBD as a systemic immunometabolic modulator.

papers.title: Homoeopathic Management of Hypothyroidism: A Narrative Review of Reported Clinical Experience, Individualised Prescribing, and Research Gaps.
papers.summary: This narrative review of 53 sources found that the available evidence on homoeopathic management of hypothyroidism is heterogeneous and predominantly uncontrolled, with reported improvements that cannot be assumed to represent treatment-specific effects. The authors conclude that a scientifically established mechanism for specific clinical effects has not been demonstrated and that homoeopathic care should not replace or delay indicated thyroid hormone therapy.

papers.title: Motives and Sources for Prescription Opioid Misuse Among Adolescents and Young Adults With Criminal Justice System Contact.
papers.summary: Analyzed National Survey on Drug Use and Health (2015–2019) data to examine associations between criminal justice system contact and prescription opioid misuse motives and sources among adolescents and young adults. Those with criminal justice contact were more likely to report recreational or sleep/relaxation motives and, among young adults, non-medical sources such as free, purchase, or theft, identifying them as a high-need population.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
